questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, then select the option "No error".**

Although people had been on watch and/ the watchkeepers were very tired,/ everyone were up and buzzing.

options.text: Although people had been on watch and

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 4'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The part of the sentence that contains a **grammatical error** is:** everyone were up and buzzing.**
 
• The** error lies in** the verb agreement.
 
• **The subject** "everyone" is singular and hence should be followed by a** singular verb form** "was" instead of the plural form "were".
 
• **Everyone was up and buzzing: **This phrase suggests that all people (perhaps referring to the people on watch and the watchkeepers) were awake (up) and active or excited (buzzing).

Therefore, he **corrected sentence **would be:* "Although people had been on watch and the watchkeepers were very tired, **everyone was up and buzzing."***

questions.question:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Pick the option that gives their correct order.

P. Fasting also leads to a feeling of rejuvenation and extended life expectancy.

Q. This might be due to the detoxification effect of fasting.

R. A study was performed on earthworms that showed the extension of life thanks to fasting.

S. The experiment was performed in the 1930s by isolating one worm and putting it on a cycle of fasting and feeding.

The isolated worm outlived the other worms by 19 generations, while still maintaining its freshness and youthful physiological characteristics.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 1'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The sentences follow a logical flow, **starting with the general concept of fasting** leading to a feeling of rejuvenation and extended life expectancy (P).
 
• Then** it introduces a possible reason for this effect, **which is the detoxification effect of fasting (Q).
 
• The sentence **then provides specific evidence of a study** performed on earthworms that showed the extension of life due to fasting (R).
 
• **Finally, it describes the experiment** performed in the 1930s, isolating one worm and observing its extended lifespan and maintained youthful characteristics (S).

The** correct arrangement** is as follows:

 
• **P. **Fasting also leads to a feeling of rejuvenation and extended life expectancy.
 
• **Q.** This might be due to the detoxification effect of fasting.
 
• **R.** A study was performed on earthworms that showed the extension of life thanks to fasting.
 
• **S.** The experiment was performed in the 1930s by isolating one worm and putting it on a cycle of fasting and feeding.
 
• The isolated worm outlived the other worms by 19 generations while still maintaining its freshness and youthful physiological characteristics.

Therefore, the** correct order **is: **'PQRS'.**

questions.question:
**Direction: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, then select the option "No error".**

The credit for organising/ the successful event was/ given to both Neha and I.

options.text: given to both Neha and I.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 3'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The part of the sentence that contains a **grammatical error** is: **given to both Neha and I.**
 
• In this case, **"I" **should be replaced with **"me."** The pronoun** "I" **is **used as **a subject, while "me" is used as an object.
 
• When you remove "Neha and," it becomes clear that "me" is the correct form to use: **"The credit...was given to me."**
 
• **Given to both Neha and me:** This indicates that the credit (or recognition) for organizing the successful event was attributed to both Neha and the speaker.

Therefore, the **corrected sentence** is:* "The credit for organizing the successful event was **given to both Neha and me.**"*

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the most suitable word.

He made me think of an old time magician more than ______ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 2' **i.e.** 'Anything'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **In this context,** **"anything"** is the most suitable choice** because** it implies that out of all possible comparisons, the most fitting one is an old-time magician.
 
• The word** "anything" **is often** used in **comparative structures to mean "any other thing."

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is:* He made me think of an old time magician more than **anything.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Here is a brief explanation of the **other options**:

 
 
• **A thing: **This is grammatically correct, but it sounds somewhat unnatural in this context. It doesn't have the same emphasis as "anything."
 
• **Everything: **This doesn't make logical sense in this context because it implies that he made the speaker think of an old-time magician more than all things combined, which is likely not the intended meaning.
 
• **Something:** This could potentially work, but "anything" is a more common choice in comparative structures and sounds more natural in this sentence.

• Finally,** S concludes the sentence **by providing additional context and detail, specifying that it is the indirect effects experienced from long periods of volcanic unrest that are not receiving adequate assistance.
